surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Flames handle the Ducks
paras: The Ducks’ Roger McQueen played his first NHL game. Adam Klapka struck first for the Flames midway through the first. Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson scored 1:56 apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Aydar Suniev tied it 2-2 midway through the second. Martin Pospíšil put the Flames ahead for good with 4:22 left. Yegor Sharangovich added the empty-netter with 1:22 left to make it 4-2.

The Flames had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Ducks 36-25. Wolf shook off a shaky start for the Flames, allowing two goals on the first seven shots and none on the last 18, and Lukáš Dostál stopped 32 of 35.
Jeff Malott and Klapka squared off midway through the second. The Flames improved to 1-5-0, and the Ducks dropped to 4-2-0.

items.text: The Flames won for the first time this season, in their sixth game.
Leo Carlsson extended his point streak against Calgary to six games.
Jackson LaCombe’s five-game point streak ended.
Martin Pospíšil scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 5 (17 games played since).
